standard.coverage: Most employers (6 or more employees, non-seasonal).
standard.note: N.J.S.A. 34:11-56a4 -- the post-$15 phase of the 2019 Raise the Wage Act, now on annual CPI indexing. 2027: $16.48 (see provisional.updatedFor2027).

tipped.note: New Jersey's tipped cash wage steps with the standard rate.

variants.label: Seasonal employers and employers with fewer than 6 employees
variants.test: N.J.S.A. 34:11-56a4. This tier is still CATCHING UP to the main rate and converges later in the schedule.

variants.label: Agricultural employees
variants.test: A separate, slower schedule for farm workers.

variants.label: Direct care staff at long-term care facilities

sources.title: NJDOL press release 2026-09-29 -- minimum wage to increase to $16.48 on Jan. 1
sources.verifiedBy: Read directly 2026-10-25: standard $16.48; seasonal/small employers $16.25; long-term-care direct care $19.48; agricultural $15.00; tipped cash wage $6.61 with the maximum tip credit unchanged at $9.87.

sources.title: U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division -- State Minimum Wage Laws (table current as of July 1, 2026)

DOL's own state-by-state table is the spine of every standard rate in this database; where a state's own labor department was ALSO read directly, that source is listed too and wins on any disagreement (see South Dakota's tipped cash wage for the one case where they disagreed).

sources.title: New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development -- minimum wage increase announcement for January 1, 2026
sources.verifiedBy: cross_source_confirmed this session for $15.92 general, $15.23 seasonal/small, $14.20 agricultural and the $6.05 tipped cash wage. DOL's own tables independently carry $15.92 / $15.23 / $6.05.

sources.title: New Jersey Office of Administrative Law -- Notice of Administrative Changes, Minimum Wage (N.J.A.C. 12:56-3.1/3.2/3.3), filed 2025-09-26
sources.verifiedBy: PDF downloaded and its text extracted directly this session. Confirms the CPI-W (U.S. City Average) methodology verbatim and the exact underlying index values: 'the CPI-W, U.S. City Average, in August 2024 was 308.640, and in August 2025 it was 317.306 ... an increase of 2.81 percent.' 2.81% applied to 2025's $15.49 general rate computes to $15.92 (matches this file's own figure); the document's later pages, where the per-category dollar figures for 2026 presumably appear, did not extract as readable text this pass -- those figures rest on the NJDOL press-release citation already carried above.

knownGaps: The long-term-care direct-care premium ($3.00 over the state rate) is cross-sourced rather than read off NJDOL's own page this pass.
